claim: In dino-autofocus's focus sweep, a frame whose mean brightness departs from the sweep's median frame mean by more than the caller's tolerance, taken as a fraction of that median, is treated as a light dropout rather than a focus change: it is dropped before the peak is located and cannot be chosen.
validity_conditions: A classical sharpness metric of one monochrome widefield frame as read, clipped pixels not masked. It ranks frames of one sweep against each other; it says nothing about which plane holds the sample, and its value is not comparable across metrics or across sweeps taken with different exposure or binning. Corrected from the drafted sentence, which did not say the tolerance is relative to the median; the code compares the absolute departure with the tolerance times the median. 10.2.1: TRANSFER. Place: a store entry -- the one place 10.2's 2026-10-03 paragraph opens for dino-autofocus before 11-24 designs the focus search, so that design can cite the method without any code having crossed. Rule: 10.3 rule 1, capped at E3 as a run taken in another project. No figure crosses (rules 3 and 4): every threshold the method uses is its caller's argument and none is entered. It says what the method IS at the pinned commit, not that it works on this stand.

valid_until.no_event: The claim describes one file at one commit, identified by its LF-normalised body sha256, so nothing ends it. A later change to that file in dino-autofocus is a new source, and the entry describing it supersedes this one.
